prompt: Algae grow in Lake Fenby, where the water holds very little phosphorus, a mineral nutrient. Heavy rains then wash phosphorus-rich fertilizer from nearby farms into the lake. What will most likely happen to the algae over the next few weeks?
choices: The algae will stay the same, because algae make all their food from sunlight.
The algae will decrease, because any fertilizer from a farm poisons living things.
The algae will be back to normal within a day, because a lake keeps its own balance.
The algae will probably increase, because more of a nutrient they lacked is now in the water.
correct_answer: The algae will probably increase, because more of a nutrient they lacked is now in the water.
explanation: Phosphorus was in short supply, so it limited how much the algae could grow; adding it removes that limit and the algae population grows.

distractor_rationales.choice: The algae will stay the same, because algae make all their food from sunlight.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: algae need only sunlight; they also need mineral nutrients such as phosphorus, so adding it lets them grow
distractor_rationales.misconception: students think producers need only sunlight, not minerals, to grow

distractor_rationales.choice: The algae will decrease, because any fertilizer from a farm poisons living things.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: fertilizer poisons algae; fertilizer supplies the nutrients that plants and algae use
distractor_rationales.misconception: students think any farm chemical harms every living thing it reaches

distractor_rationales.choice: The algae will be back to normal within a day, because a lake keeps its own balance.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: a lake restores its balance at once; the added phosphorus stays in the water and fuels growth for weeks
distractor_rationales.misconception: students think nature keeps populations in balance, so a lake quickly returns to normal on its own

real_world_check: When a limiting nutrient such as phosphorus is added to a lake, algae populations can grow quickly, forming an algal bloom.
